# Independent ZIP compatibility fixtures

These public inert archives are authored with Python 3.13's standard-library
`zipfile`, independently of the Rust ZIP dependency under test. Regenerate with
`python core/tests/fixtures/zip-compat/generate.py` from the repository root.
Normal Cargo tests consume the committed bytes and do not require Python.
No upstream download, private profile, installed browser or actual executable is
included. `browser.exe` is a text marker and is never executed. The `.sf` file
is a text layout marker, not a valid cryptographic signature.

`flat.zip` has root-level browser/extension-shaped entries. `wrapped-stream.zip`
has the same entries below `bundle/`, written to a nonseekable stream with data
descriptors. Both contain Stored, Deflate, Bzip2 and LZMA payloads, a UTF-8 path,
an empty directory and a small entry with a forced ZIP64 local header. These
exercise byte-preserving extraction and wrapper handling in both consumers;
the flat layout additionally exercises the XPI signature-file presence check.
This is not native browser startup, all-format interoperability or signature
validation. The XPI checker intentionally inspects layout only.

`corrupt-crc.zip` flips one byte of the stored browser marker without updating
its CRC; browser/extension extraction must return an error. `truncated.zip`
contains the first half of the flat archive and must be refused by all three
consumers. These tests complement the existing path traversal, reparse-point,
size-budget, verification and transaction-preservation tests.

A trial strict-UTF8 rejection fixture was removed: ZIP 9 retains CP437 fallback
for non-UTF8 filename bytes. No strict-UTF8 promise is made; fallible filename
API errors are propagated rather than replaced with a permissive fallback.

The following identities record the committed generated bytes. Regeneration on
another Python/compression-library version may differ; inspect changes instead
of silently accepting new hashes.
